title: Marcos flies to China for APEC Summit
summary: President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. on Wednesday afternoon left Manila to participate in the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders" Meeting in Shenzhen, China.

blocks.text: President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. on Wednesday afternoon left Manila to participate in the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders’ Meeting in Shenzhen, China.
The PR001 carrying the President and his delegation left Villamor Air Base at 3: p.m.

With Marcos are First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos, Finance Secretary Frederick Go, Trade and Industry Secretary Cristina Roque, Foreign Affairs Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro, and Presidential Communications Office Secretary Lino Cayetano.
They are expected to land at Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport past 5 p.m.
The APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting (AELM) from November 18 to 19 will be held in Shenzhen, which is widely known as the Silicon Valley of China.
In his departure message, Marcos committed to upholding national interest even as he intends to engage with China “constructively” to expand trade and investment amid the APEC Summit.

“We will engage China constructively on expanding trade, investment, and people-to-people exchanges that benefit our peoples, even as we remain steadfast in upholding our national interest,” the President said.
“Our message is clear—the Philippines is open for business. Invest in the Filipino,” he added.
Marcos also said his attendance at the AELM and other related activities was upon the invitation of Chinese President Xi Jinping.
Under the theme “Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together,” the APEC Summit this year focuses on three key priorities: openness, innovation, and cooperation.

Marcos’ visit to China came after the Philippines hosted the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit and Related Summits, which was attended by several regional and world leaders, including US President Donald Trump.
Trump is also set to fly to China following his visit to Malacañang Palace on Wednesday. —AOL, GMA News
